fact_en: Want to compare the thickness of the main stem? Just wrap a string around it and measure the string!
fact_bis: Aron itandi ang kabag-on sa pangunang punoan, magpulupot lang og pisi libot niini ug sukda ang pisi!

findings.note: title_bis "Gibag-on sa Lihog" for "Stem Thickness": lihog is not a plant part in Cebuano (it is the request/favour root of palihog); the thing being measured is unnamed in the title. The card's own body uses the correct word — "kabag-on sa pangunang punoan" — which marks the title as the outlier.

fact_en:
What is inside the tropical rainforest biome in the Philippines?

It contains many different ecosystems, from mountain forests to lowland swamps, all working together in nature!
fact_bis:
Unsa ang naa sa tropical rainforest biome sa Pilipinas?

Adunay daghang lain-laing ecosystem, gikan sa gubat sa bukid hangtod sa lamakan sa ubos nga lugar!

findings.note: title_en 'Biome & Ecosystems'; English body lists ecosystems 'from mountain forests to lowland swamps'. The Cebuano renders mountain forests as 'gikan sa gubat sa bukid' — in Cebuano gubat means WAR (Tagalog false friend; Cebuano forest is lasang/kalasangan). The card never says lasang anywhere, and 'rainforest' appears only untranslated in English, so nothing on the card corrects it: a child reading only the Cebuano is told a rainforest biome contains ecosystems ranging 'from the war in the mountain to the lowland swamp', losing the mountain-forest half of the example entirely. Corpus evidence: forest cards use lasang (237) / kalasangan (173) / kagubatan (76), while standalone gubat elsewhere in this same corpus is correctly the war sense (ffct-26273 submarine 'gigamit sa gubat', ffct-12088 'gubat sa lawas batok sa impeksyon', ffct-00702 'Gubat sa Liog').

fact_en:
How does long DNA fit inside a tiny nucleus?

It wraps around proteins called histones, just like thread winding around tiny spools to stay tidy!
fact_bis:
Unsaon pagkasya sa taas nga DNA sa sulod sa gamay nga nucleus?

Mobakos kini sa mga protina nga gitawag og histones, sama sa hilo nga molikop sa gagmay nga spools aron magpabiling limpyo!

findings.note: Body: "sama sa hilo nga molikop sa gagmay nga spools" for English "like thread winding around tiny spools". In Cebuano hilo = POISON (Spanish/other-language 'hilo' = thread; Cebuano thread is tanod). The card never uses the right word anywhere, so the whole analogy for DNA/histone packing reads as 'poison winding around spools'. Confirmed false-friend class. Note the core claim (DNA wraps around proteins called histones) does survive, so this is a defective analogy rather than a lost headline fact — lower severity than a number or direction error.

fact_en: When DNA is heated, the weak bonds between the two strands break, and the double helix unwinds into two separate strands!
fact_bis: Kung mainitan ang DNA, ang huyang nga mga koneksyon tali sa duha ka hilo maputol, ug ang double helix mobuklad ngadto sa duha ka bulag nga hilo!

findings.note: Heat Denaturation. EN "the weak bonds between the two strands break, and the double helix unwinds into two separate strands" -> BIS uses "hilo" for strand twice: "tali sa duha ka hilo maputol ... ngadto sa duha ka bulag nga hilo". In Cebuano hilo = POISON (strand/fibre is hibla); nothing in the card restores it, so the only noun naming what DNA separates into is a different thing. Sibling card ffct-38235 in the same batch gets it right (title "Duha ka Hibla sa DNA", body "strand"), which is the evidence this card is the outlier.

fact_en: Over time, wind, water, and temperature changes break rocks into smaller pieces that become part of the soil!
fact_bis: Sa paglabay sa panahon, ang hangin, tubig, ug pagbag-o sa temperature mabuak ang mga bato ug mahimong parte sa yuta!

findings.note: title_bis "Paghuyhoy sa Bato" for "Weathering". Cebuano huyhoy/huyuhoy = a gentle BREEZE, not weathering (pag-agnas / pagkaagnas sa bato); the title names a different thing and the body never names the process at all (it only describes wind, water and temperature breaking rocks), so the Cebuano term a child carries away from this card is wrong. Same wrong-word family as the confirmed hubas/uwang substitutions for weathering and erosion.

fact_en: If cooking when shaking begins, turn off the stove if you can reach it safely, then drop, cover, and hold!
fact_bis: Kung nagluto kung magsugod ang linog, palonga ang kalan kung maabot nga luwas, dayon duko, tago, ug kumot!

findings.note: "drop, cover, and hold" -> "duko, tago, ug kumot". Cebuano kumot = to crumple/rumple (Tagalog kumot = blanket); it is not "hold on", which is kapyot/kupot/gunit. The third step of the core safety drill becomes a nonsense action and nothing else in the card restores it, so a child reading only the Cebuano cannot know what to do after taking cover. The same batch uses the correct verb elsewhere ("Kupti kini..." in ffct-38497, "Kupti ang matag usa..." in ffct-38501), so this card is the outlier.

fact_en:
How can you compare the density of two rocks?

Hold one in each hand to feel which is heavier for its size, or use a balance scale!
fact_bis:
Unsaon pagtandi sa density sa duha ka bato?

Kupti ang matag usa sa imong kamot para bantayan kung asa ang mas bug-at, o gamita ang balance scale!

findings.note: "which is heavier for its size" -> "kung asa ang mas bug-at" (simply "which is heavier"). The per-size qualifier is the entire density concept and is not restored anywhere on the card, so the Cebuano answer to its own question ("Unsaon pagtandi sa density sa duha ka bato?") teaches the false rule heavier = denser. Cebuano-only child ends up with weight, not density.

fact_en:
What is a plate boundary?

It’s the meeting line where two moving pieces of Earth's crust touch! Most earthquakes and volcanoes happen here.
fact_bis:
Unsa ang plate boundary?

Kini ang linya diin nagtagbo ang duha ka naglihok nga piraso sa Earth's crust! Dinhi kanunay mahitabo ang linog ug bolkan.

findings.note: title_bis "Utlanan sa Plato" = "edge of the dinner plate" in Cebuano; plato is the everyday word for a dish (Tagalog science's "tektonikong plato" does not carry over). The card's own body keeps the correct English "plate boundary" / "piraso sa Earth's crust", and every sibling card in the same series titles it "Plate" (ffct-38876 "Katulin sa Plate", ffct-38877 "Mga Lakang sa Plate", ffct-38878 "Calculator sa Plate"), so this title is the outlier. Same corpus even uses plato correctly for a real dish two cards earlier (ffct-38834, syrup poured sa plato).

fact_en: Earth's outer shell is like a giant puzzle! It has about seven large plates and smaller ones, all moving at different speeds.
fact_bis: Ang gawas nga panit sa Earth sama sa giant puzzle! Aduna kini pito ka dagkong plate ug gagmay, tanan naglihok sa lain-laing katulin.

findings.note: title_bis "Pangunang Plato" reads as "main dinner plate" for "Major Plates"; Cebuano plato = dish, not a tectonic plate. The card's own body uses the correct word ("pito ka dagkong plate"), confirming the title is the defective field.

fact_en: Hard-working muscle cells have way more mitochondria than fat cells because they need extra energy to contract and move!
fact_bis: Ang masipag nga muscle cells adunay mas daghan nga mitochondria kaysa sa fat cells kay kinahanglan nila ug extra energy para mokontra!

findings.note: "kinahanglan nila ug extra energy para mokontra" — Cebuano mokontra = to oppose / go against, not to contract a muscle (pagkuyos / pag-urong sa kaunoran). Wrong-sense verb: the child is told muscle cells spend energy "to oppose" something; "and move" is dropped too, and nothing in the card restores the idea that muscles shorten/contract.

fact_en: Treating the Philippines as one rigid plate is just an approximation — GNSS already shows internal deformation that careful methods include!
fact_bis: Ang pagtratar sa Pilipinas isip usa ka rigid plate kay approximation lang — gipakita na sa GNSS ang internal deformation nga giapil sa mabinantayon nga pamaagi!

findings.note: Title_bis "Gahi nga Plato" = "rigid DINNER PLATE"; the card is about treating the Philippines as one rigid tectonic plate. The card's own body keeps the correct English "rigid plate", so the title is the outlier. plato = dinner plate is on the confirmed false-friend list for this corpus.

fact_en:
Do faster vibrating electromagnetic waves carry more energy?

Yes! Electromagnetic waves that vibrate more times per second, meaning higher frequency, carry more energy than slower ones.
fact_bis:
Mas daghan ba og energy ang mas paspas nga electromagnetic waves?

Oo! Ang electromagnetic waves nga mas paspas mo-vibrate kada segundo o mas taas nga frequency nagdala og mas daghan nga energy kaysa sa mas hinay.

findings.note: Title_bis "Paghan-ay sa Alon" = "ARRANGING/ordering of waves", a different concept from Wave Frequency (the card is about vibrations per second and energy). Unique in the corpus: every other frequency card uses kasubsob, dalas, prekwensiya or plain "Frequency" — including ffct-39004 "Dalas sa Microwave" in this same batch.
